fullPassage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.

❌ ② 측정하다 — 측정하다: (B)에서 정부가 도입한 것은 조치이므로 측정이 아님
❌ ③ 조치 — 조치: (A)에서 연구가 횟수를 측정하므로 조치가 아님
✅ ④ 측정하다 — 조치: (A) 미소 횟수를 측정(measure), (B) 대기 오염 감소를 위한 조치(measure) ←정답
det.tip: measure: (A) 측정하다 (동사) / (B) 조치, 방안 (명사)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a person who habitually delays or postpones tasks"

det.analysis:
✅ ① procrastinator: 습관적으로 일을 미루는 사람 ←정답
❌ ② respondent: 응답자 — 설문에 답하는 사람
❌ ③ interaction: 상호작용 — 사람이 아님
❌ ④ consistency: 일관성 — 사람이 아님
det.tip: procrastinator = 미루는 사람 (procrastinate=미루다 + -or=~하는 사람)

questions.passage: Respondents' __________ (recollect) may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: recollect(동사: 기억해내다) → recollections(명사: 기억들): Respondents' 뒤에 소유격이므로 명사 필요. 복수형 recollections.
det.tip: 동사 → 명사: recollect → recollection(s). 소유격(') 뒤에는 명사가 온다.

questions.passage: Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure __________ (consistent) from one study to the next.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: consistent(형용사: 일관된) → consistency(명사: 일관성): ensure 뒤에 목적어(명사)가 필요. 형용사를 명사형으로 변환.
det.tip: 형용사 → 명사: consistent → consistency. ensure + 명사 구조.

questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" __________. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 prompts a concrete answer(구체적인 답변을 유도한다)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① yields quantitative data: 정량적 데이터를 산출한다 — 앞 문장과 중복되며 맥락에 부적합
❌ ② varies widely among people: 사람들 사이에서 크게 다르다 — 문맥상 '슬퍼서 병가를 냈느냐'는 구체적 답을 유도하므로 부적합
✅ ③ prompts a concrete answer: 구체적인 답변을 유도한다 — 모호한 질문 대신 구체적 질문이 구체적 답변을 유도한다는 맥락 ←정답
❌ ④ ensures research consistency: 연구 일관성을 보장한다 — 마지막 문장 내용이므로 이 위치에 부적합
det.tip: But asking '...sad enough to call in sick to work?' prompts a concrete answer — 추상적 질문 vs 구체적 질문의 대비

questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make __________ and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 abstract concepts clearer(추상적 개념을 더 명확하게)가 적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① abstract concepts clearer: 추상적 개념을 더 명확하게 만든다 — 구체적 질문이 추상적 개념을 명확히 한다는 글의 결론 ←정답
❌ ② quantitative data reliable: 정량적 데이터를 신뢰할 수 있게 — help make의 목적어로 부적합한 맥락
❌ ③ concrete responses accurate: 구체적 응답을 정확하게 — 이미 concrete이므로 의미 중복
❌ ④ research definitions broader: 연구 정의를 더 넓게 — 글의 결론과 반대 방향
det.tip: Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer — 구체적 질문 → 추상적 개념 명확화라는 글의 핵심 주장
